summary: Just-in-time join access for suspected cross-customer output sharing investigation
description:
Issue summary: Customer A flagged that a subset of model outputs contained text fragments that match proprietary prompts/data from Customer B. Impact: potential cross-customer leakage of user-provided content. Request: short, tightly scoped join of inference request traces with audit log events and K/V cache slice metadata to verify whether outputs were generated from the same originating prompt or from a shared cached prefix. Goal is to determine scope and provide an initial remediation plan.

Justification: initial triage by Customer Success shows repeated unique identifier strings appearing across tenants. We need to confirm whether this is due to a serving-layer cache miskeying, a model artifact, or an ingestion issue. Existing dashboards do not expose the combined correlation view required for this analysis without privileged access to raw request traces and cache keys.

Scope: time range 2026-03-08T00:00:00Z -> 2026-03-09T12:00:00Z, tenant IDs: tenant-A (customer A) and tenant-B (customer B). Minimum fields: request_id, epoch_ts, model_version, route, cached_prefix_hash (redacted), output_snippet (redacted to 64 chars), kv_cache_segment_id (redacted). No full plaintext payloads to be exported.

Controls requested: 1) 8-hour window of privileged read-only access for 3 engineers (Diego Marquez, Priya Rao, and Helena Ortiz) via just-in-time (JIT) ephemeral role bindings; 2) dual-approval: SRE lead + Security; 3) all queries executed through sandboxed query runner with automatic redaction hooks; 4) results to be stored for 48 hours in a KMS-encrypted bucket with access logged and post-access attestation.

Retention and follow-up: export artifacts will be certified by Security and deleted after 48 hours unless legal escalates. Any findings that indicate systemic risk will trigger a separate incident ticket with remediation and rollout notes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Confirm customer-reported output examples (attached sample hashes). 2) Request join query: inference_traces JOIN audit_events on request_id with filter on tenant_A/tenant_B and time window. 3) Apply redaction UDFs to mask PII and truncate outputs to 64 characters. 4) Inspect cache segment IDs and kernel selection metadata for collisions. 5) If matching cache keys found, snapshot minimal key metadata only (no plaintext) for further root cause analysis.
logs: Relevant dashboards: /dashboards/serving/kv-cache-evictions, /dashboards/audit/request-latency spikes. Quick links: grafana: grafana.redwood.internal/d/kvcache?var-region=us-west, splunk query: index=prod inference request_id IN (list). Sample request_ids provided in attachments.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:40 - Diego: initial tail of logs shows two near-identical outputs for different tenant IDs within the same 2s window on host gpu-05. 2026-03-10 10:12 - Priya: bootstrapped join locally using anonymized request_ids; no obvious model-level reuse visible in top-level traces. 2026-03-11 15:00 - Helena: identified overlapping cache segment ids but could not correlate to tenant scoping without privileged mapping. Hypothesis: possible cache-key namespace collision when prefix hashing handled by older runtime kernel on that host. Next: request JIT join to validate mapping between segment and tenant.

- Dual-approval (SRE lead + Security)
- Queries run through redaction-enabled sandbox
- Export retention: 48 hours max, KMS-encrypted, access logged

resolution: (Pending) Awaiting Security dual-approval and SRE owner to provision JIT bindings. If approved, execute scoped join and deliver findings. Any confirmed leakage will result in an Incident (P0) and immediate cache invalidation and targeted rollback of the suspect runtime kernel.
